chunk_findings.detail: `_progress` now caches and returns one mutable `say` closure per `progressToken`, and line 909 gives that same closure to `heartbeat`. The heartbeat timer must call `say` from a second thread while `_invoke` also calls it for each emitted line, but `count[0] += 1` inside `say` is an unsynchronized read-modify-write. Example: `count[0]` is 10; the heartbeat thread reads 10; the main thread processes two output lines and emits progress 11 and 12; the heartbeat thread then stores 11 and emits `progress: 11` after `12` for the same `progressToken`, so progress decreases, violating MCP's monotonic progress requirement. The counter and send must be serialized with a lock.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:_progress (shared with heartbeats)

chunk_findings.detail: `heartbeat` only rejects `every <= 0`; it never checks `math.isfinite(every)`. If `every` is `float("nan")` — either via `[mcp] progress_s = nan` (a valid TOML float) or by a caller passing `heartbeat(..., every=float("nan"))` — the guard passes, a thread is started, and `done.wait(every)` does not sleep (CPython's condition wait treats NaN as non-positive), so the `while not done.wait(every): say(...)` loop becomes a busy spin that floods `notifications/progress` and pegs a CPU for the duration of the call.

chunk_findings.detail: When a pending release/upgrade notice exists, `START.is_measuring()` makes the release-notice function return `""`, so the pending notice text is omitted from the `brief --for-agent` output while `doctor` is measuring the session start cost. The early return also prevents `US.take_for_brief` from consuming the notice, so a real subsequent session start will still include it. Given a pending notice and a context budget set just above the measured cost without the notice, `doctor` reports under budget, but the actual first-turn brief exceeds the budget. This under-counts a component that the intent explicitly says to count (`brief --for-agent`) and defeats the over-budget warning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:202

chunk_findings.detail: The new `[session].context_budget_tokens` knob documents its measured scope as “the MCP instructions, `tools/list` for the active `[mcp].tools` profile and the session brief,” but the stated intent for this change says the measurement also includes `hooks session-start output`. A user configuring the budget from this doc will not account for session-start hooks; when a hook emits a large start payload, the actual measured cost exceeds their budget even though the doc led them to believe it was excluded, producing a false `OVER` warning. The doc should mention hooks session-start output.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/session.py:99

chunk_findings.detail: `report()` is the function that actually builds the texts by calling `start_texts(repo, agent)`, but it never enters the `measuring()` context manager. The module docstring says `measuring()` exists so once-per-version notices are not consumed and the brief does no housekeeping while a text is built. Since `report()` calls `start_texts()` at line 102 with `is_measuring()` still False, the first measurement will run those side effects: an upgrade notice guarded by `is_measuring()` will be consumed, later measurements/builds will omit it, and the reported session start cost will change between runs. The call should be wrapped in `with measuring():`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:report

chunk_findings.detail: The stated intent is to count bytes and estimate tokens as bytes/4, but `measure()` uses `len(text)` (Unicode code points) for both `chars` and `parts`. For a start text of 400 `'é'` characters at the default ratio 4, the code records `chars=400` and `tokens=100`, whereas the required byte count is 800 UTF-8 bytes and the byte/4 estimate is 200 tokens. Non-ASCII start-text content will understate the session start cost and can hide an over-budget condition.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:measure

chunk_findings.detail: When `startcost_texts.start_texts` measures the MCP initialize instructions, it runs inside `SC.measuring()`. This change makes the notice builder return `""` in that state so the doctor measurement does not consume the one-time `upgrade_start`/`upgrade_notice`/`release_proposal` notice. But if such a notice is pending, it is still present for the real session that follows, so the actual first-turn instructions will include its text while the measured `texts["instructions"]` does not. For example, a repo with a large pending `release_proposal` can make `ddflow doctor` report “session start cost: N tokens” under budget when the subsequent real start exceeds it, defeating the over-budget warning.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:1226

chunk_findings.detail: Previous findings 1 and 5 still hold and are not answered by the added documentation probe. `report()` now deliberately builds `start_texts(repo, agent)` inside `measuring()`, so the one-time `upgrade_start`/`upgrade_notice`/`release_proposal` notice is omitted from the measured `instructions`/brief text to avoid consuming it, while a real subsequent session start will still include that notice. chunk_findings.detail: The added `if SC.is_measuring(): return ""` is still present. `ddflow/surfaces/startcost_texts.start_texts` builds the MCP instructions inside `with SC.measuring()`, so a pending one-time `upgrade_start`/`upgrade_notice`/`release_proposal` notice is omitted from the measured `texts["instructions"]`. Input: pending notice costs 1,200 tokens, steady-state measured instructions/tools/brief cost 1,000, and `session.context_budget_tokens` is 2,000. chunk_findings.detail: The upgrade notice announces the ratio knob as `session.start_chars_per_token` and says it is “The characters-per-token ratio of the session start cost estimate,” but the accepted cost behavior (probe `test_the_cost_is_counted_in_bytes_not_code_points`) counts UTF-8 bytes, not code points. For non-ASCII start text, those units differ: 400 `'é'` characters at the default `4.0` are 800 bytes, so the doctor line will estimate 200 tokens even though this notice’s wording says the ratio applies to characters and implies 100. A user calibrating from this notice will set the wrong ratio; the key and `why` should say bytes-per-token if byte counting is the intended behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: The new `if START.is_measuring(): return ""` makes the measured brief omit the one-time upgrade/release notice. Because the measurement deliberately does not consume the notice, the very next real session start still includes it, so the doctor-reported “session start cost” is lower than the actual next start by the notice text. The added `session.start_notice_reserve_tokens` knob does not fix this: this guard returns before `US.take_for_brief`/`UN.line` runs, so the actual pending notice text is never measured, and a fixed operator-set reserve can be smaller than the notice (including 0). Input: pending notice costs 1,200 tokens, the other start texts cost 1,000, `context_budget_tokens = 1100`, and the reserve is set below 200; doctor reports 1,000 and does not warn, but the next real session start uses 2,200 tokens. This is the same undercount as prior findings #1/#2, now also encoded for the brief’s upgrade/release notice.

chunk_findings.detail: `if rep.problem or not rep.stale: return ""` suppresses the precheck whenever `regenerate_pins` reports any problem, even if `rep.stale` is non-empty. In that case `_stale_pins` returns `""`, `run` proceeds to the full suite, and the stale pin is not named before the run — exactly the failure mode this change is meant to prevent. chunk_findings.detail: If `regenerate_pins` reports both an uncheckable pin and a stale pin, the precheck incorrectly does nothing. The condition `if rep.problem or not rep.stale:` is truthy whenever `rep.problem` is truthy, even if `rep.stale` is also non-empty, so `_stale_pins` returns `""`. Concrete failure: one recipe times out/becomes uncheckable (`rep.problem` non-empty) while the README knob/command table is stale (`rep.stale` non-empty). The stale pin is not named, the gate proceeds to the full suite, and then fails with the exact opaque failure this change is meant to prevent. This contradicts the knob doc that an uncheckable pin is skipped, never a failure; skipping one uncheckable pin should not suppress other stale pins that were successfully checked.

chunk_findings.detail: If a gate record has a truthy whitespace-only `reason` (e.g. `"   "`), `unavailable_reasons` skips the `or "no reason was recorded"` fallback, then `" ".join("   ".split())` produces `""` and stores an empty `why[g]`. `render()` only tests `if g in self.why`, not whether the value is non-empty, so the output line becomes `  unavailable ci  -- ` with a dangling separator instead of saying no reason was recorded. The fallback should be applied after normalization, or `render()` should ignore empty `why` values.

chunk_findings.detail: `_unavailable_reasons` still assumes `rec.reason` is a string whenever `rec` exists, despite the docstring saying records from before the mandatory-reason rule "show as having none." If `it.gates` returns a record whose `reason` is `None` (the usual Python value for "no reason recorded"), `(rec.reason if rec else "")` evaluates to `None`, so `None.split()` raises `AttributeError`; `gate status` crashes instead of printing `"no reason was recorded"`. chunk_findings.detail: The previous undercount finding still holds. While `START.is_measuring()` is true, this returns `""` instead of the release/upgrade notice text; `start_texts` measures the plain `brief(...)` path that the session-start hook prints (per the prior probe), so a pending first-run notice is omitted from the doctor's session-start cost. Concrete: a 0.1.3-built repo has an untaken release proposal carrying the 1,200-token notice; `ddflow doctor` starts measuring, `_upgrade_notice_for_start` returns `""`, and the reported cost is the components plus the unhooked brief, so it does not warn even when that 1,200-token notice would make the real first turn exceed `session.context_budget_tokens`. The cited probe materialising the notice from a 0.1.3-built project does not exercise this measuring branch and therefore does not answer this code path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/brief.py:_upgrade_notice_for_start

chunk_findings.detail: The previous undercount finding still holds. `measure` adds only a fixed `reserve` token count when `parts` is non-empty, rather than measuring the actual pending upgrade notice text. A pending notice of 1,200 tokens with `[session].start_notice_reserve_tokens` set to 64 (or 0) is still undercounted by the remaining 1,136 tokens, because the actual notice is never built and only the fixed reserve is added. The probe cited in triage checks only that a specific 0.1.3-built notice fits the default reserve, not that a larger pending notice (the earlier 1,200-token `release_proposal` scenario) is covered. Additionally, if every measured text is empty, `parts` is empty and the reserve is omitted entirely, so a pending notice with no other startup texts is omitted altogether.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:89-90

chunk_findings.detail: `StartCost.chars` is documented as `name -> characters`, and `as_dict()` exposes the JSON key `"chars"`, but `measure` populates it with `len(text.encode("utf-8"))`, which is a UTF-8 byte count, not a character count. Given a brief containing "é", the report reports `chars` as 2 for that part, not 1. Downstream consumers of the JSON report will interpret the value incorrectly. The field should hold byte counts under a different name, or `chars` should be computed as an actual character count.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:86

chunk_findings.detail: The added probe still does not answer the prior undercount for a large pending `release_proposal` or MCP instruction notice. It copies a 0.1.3-built project and checks only the single `Upgraded ddflow` line length against the default reserve; it never materialises a project with a pending 1,200-token `release_proposal` and never runs the doctor-then-first-session sequence with that pending text. A repo whose pending release notice is large can therefore still exceed `reserve * bytes_per_token`, and `ddflow doctor` can still undercount the real first-turn cost while both this test and `test_the_default_reserve_covers_the_notice_lines_a_session_start_can_carry` pass.

chunk_findings.detail: The reserve represented by `[session].start_notice_reserve_tokens` is documented in `ddflow/config_sections/session.py` as applying to "the one-line upgrade or release notice that leads the first session after an upgrade." But `measure` adds that fixed reserve whenever `parts` is non-empty, so any ordinary session with MCP instructions, `tools/list`, or a brief and no pending release/upgrade notice is also charged 100 default tokens for a notice that will never be printed. The probe cited for the previous undercount finding only checks that the real one-line notice fits under the default reserve; it does not cover the no-notice case. Concrete: run `ddflow doctor` on a current-version repo whose `tools/list` text alone measures as `context_budget_tokens - 50` tokens; the doctor line reports OVER because the 100-token reserve is added even though no pending notice exists.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow.services.startcost.measure

chunk_findings.detail: `measure`'s reserve guard uses the truthiness of the `parts` dict, but `parts` contains an entry for every key in `texts` even when that entry is 0 tokens. For example, `measure({"brief": ""}, chars_per_token= [REDACTED] budget=100, reserve=64)` yields `sizes == {"brief": 0}` and `parts == {"brief": 0}`; `parts` is still truthy, so the code adds `parts["upgrade notice (reserve)"] = 64`. The resulting `StartCost` reports 64 tokens and `notes()` returns a doctor cost line even though no non-empty text was measured. If `start_texts(repo, agent)` returns an empty-string entry for a session with no launch brief, `report` will show a phantom `session start cost: 64 tokens ...` and can warn `OVER by 64` on a zero-cost session. The guard should require an actual measured contribution, such as `if reserve > 0 and any(sizes.values())`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/startcost.py:89-90

chunk_findings.detail: The test codifies that the measured `brief` is the plain session-start hook output and explicitly says it is not the subagent launch brief produced by `brief --for-agent`. That contradicts the change’s stated intent to count `brief --for-agent` as one of the first-turn costs. The launch brief can be larger than the plain hook brief, so the session-start cost meter undercounts the payload actually sent to the agent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_start_budget.py:test_the_measured_brief_is_the_one_the_session_start_hook_prints

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts that a raising cost-text builder causes `SC.report` to return a cost with empty `notes()` and empty `data()`. In `ddflow doctor`, a failure while counting MCP instructions, `tools/list`, or the brief is therefore converted into an empty/zero cost with no warning, hiding the true session-start cost. The intent says the doctor must print the line and warn over budget; silently swallowing the failure as no cost defeats that exactly when the measurement is failing.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_session_start_budget.py:test_a_failing_surface_leaves_an_empty_cost_not_a_failed_doctor

chunk_findings.detail: The test uses a freshly adopted repo, which has no pending upgrade notice, so `_upgrade_notices(...)` and `mcp._upgrade_line(...)` already return `""` outside `SC.measuring()`. The assertions inside the measuring block therefore pass even if the suppression guard is completely removed. The test does not actually exercise the once-per-version notice path it claims to protect.
